student: Llama 3.2 1B Instruct, LoRA r16, bf16 training on one A100; int4 GGUF on CPU
selection_rule:
Selection rule, written 2026-10-31 07:50 UTC, before any round-4 variant other than the rerun baseline (1b_r4_base) was scored on test or the decider's cases.
1. Within a technique (KL weight, temperature), the setting is chosen on val only: the highest agreement with each of Glimmer's val answers; a tie (within 0.3 points) goes to the lower val NLL.
2. Among the candidates (1b_v3 as served, 1b_r4_base, each technique's chosen setting, and their combination), the chosen variant is the one with the highest agreement on the decider's 196 cases against the majority of Glimmer's other answers (vs_majority_of_others, up to 5 answers per case), provided that
   (a) its test agreement with each of Glimmer's answers is at most 0.5 points below 1b_v3's (bf16, the same prompts), and
   (b) its test ECE after its own temperature scaling (fitted on val) is no worse than 1b_v3's raw test ECE.
   A difference under 1 point on the decider's cases goes to the variant with fewer order flips on the decider's cases (picks that change when the listed times are reversed).
3. The int4 file is the smallest of Q4_K_M (with and without importance matrix), Q5_K_M and Q6_K whose pick matches bf16 on at least 98% of test cases and whose paired McNemar test against bf16 (agreement with Glimmer's majority) is not significant at 0.05 on test or the decider's cases.
Caveat: the decider's cases are both a reported set and the selection criterion, so the chosen variant's number there is optimistic; val (seed 19) is the only set never used for reporting a choice.

int4.note: McNemar: a_only = bf16 right and int4 wrong, b_only = the reverse; exact two-sided p

chosen.recipe: the earlier recipe (LoRA r16, 3 epochs, cross-entropy against Glimmer's votes, letters in time order) plus one extra Glimmer answer for each of 700 random training cases (--more random ids, --kl_w 0, which with at most 2 votes per case is the same target as the votes)

recommended.why: 1.3 is the int4 file's temperature fitted on val (NLL); at 1.3, 0.55 is the operating point of 0.6 raw (decider: 76.5% answered, cascade 70.4% vs full; test 95.0% answered). The 5% conformal threshold on val is 0.79 after scaling (decider 25.5% answered).

chosen.how_chosen: by the rule written at 07:50 UTC (selection_rule), among the variants trained; the user then stopped the round before phase 2

not_run.phase2: the rationale loss, active selection (active arm alone, random+active) and the combination with order augmentation were trained part way and stopped by the user's change of plan; their Glimmer answers (583 active-arm answers, 1,275 rationales) were collected but no variant using them was scored
not_run.decider_soft_labels: not trained: the day-1 check showed the decider's order-averaged distribution agrees with Glimmer less than the student does
not_run.kl_T1: KL weights 0.5 and 0.9 at T=1 were not trained: with at most two votes per training case the majority (ties shared) equals the vote distribution, so their gradient equals KL weight 0's
not_run.int4_others: Q5_K_M and Q6_K were not measured for any variant; Q4_K_M with an importance matrix only for the rerun baseline
